subject: Renewal: Usage consolidation & staged uptick plan
messages:
From: Elena Torres <elena.torres@vitalai.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@vitalai.com
Date: 2026-10-07T08:14:00-07:00
Subject: Q3 usage report + renewal planning

Hi Jonas,

We ran the attached Q3 usage export and wanted to start the renewal conversation early. Usage spiked in September due to our new agent rollout — total token spend jumped ~62% month-over-month and we saw a small latency sensitivity on long chat sessions.

High-level ask: can Redwood help us convert this into a predictable commit that gives us headroom for growth while keeping unit costs reasonable? Procurement wants a five-line summary they can take to finance; engineering is asking whether the Dedicated headroom option or a staged commit makes more sense operationally.

I attached VitalAI_Q3_usage_report.csv for your review. Can we get a short proposal this week?

Thanks,
Elena Torres
Head of Product, VitalAI
Attachments: VitalAI_Q3_usage_report.csv (CSV, 48KB)
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Elena Torres <elena.torres@vitalai.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-08T09:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Q3 usage report + renewal planning

Hi Elena — thanks for the export and the heads-up on the agent rollout. I skimmed the CSV and pulled a few early signal points:

- Median session length tripled for your assistant flow; that increases KV-cache retention and raises per-token latency sensitivity.
- ~70% of tokens are short-form completions (fast path); 30% are long chat sessions driving peak throughput.
- Forecasting off the September spike, a straight run-rate commit would put you ~40% over commit in Q1 without staged headroom.

Proposed approach (short):
1) Staged commit with a 3-month ramp: 0->60% of Sept run-rate month 1, 80% month 2, 100% month 3.
2) Dedicated burst pool for peak chat windows (configurable autoscale + 2x burst for launch events).
3) 6-month price break for token tiers if you lock the staged commit (we'll show the unit economics).

I'll pull together a one-page ROI recap and a draft renewal proposal for your procurement team. Looping in Karthik for pricing and Marissa for rollout/ops notes. Are you available for a 30-minute sync on Tuesday 10/12?

Best,
Jonas
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachments: —
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Elena Torres <elena.torres@vitalai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-09T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Q3 usage report + renewal planning

Elena / team — attached is a short renewal proposal (redwood-inference-renewal-proposal-v2.pdf) and a token economics snapshot I created from the CSV (token-econ-snapshot.png). Key points from our side:

- Staged commit numbers: Month1 = 60% of Sept run-rate (committed), Month2 = 80%, Month3 = 100% (committed thereafter).
- Dedicated burst pool: reserved baseline for sustained throughput + pay-as-you-go burst credits for marketing spikes.
- Price tiers: 10% discount at >= monthly commit X, 18% discount at >= monthly commit Y (we mapped to your Q3 mix).
- ROI: If you adopt staged commit + burst pool, we estimate a 27% reduction in expected overage spend vs. straight run-rate with no commit; if you convert more workload to short-path generation (we can help with prompt engineering), that improves to ~33%.

Open items for procurement: 1) term length (we modeled 12 vs 24 mo), 2) enterprise clause on data retention (we have Private deployment options), 3) invoice cadence (monthly vs quarterly). I've added notes in the PDF next to each section.

Next steps:
- Confirm procurement's preferred term length and invoice cadence.
- If OK, I can generate a DocuSign-ready contract and include the burst pool addendum.
- Jonas / Marissa: schedule the Tuesday 10/12 sync (30 min) to walk through ops/rollback and SLA expectations.

Attachments: redwood-inference-renewal-proposal-v2.pdf (PDF, 180KB), token-econ-snapshot.png (PNG, 65KB)
From: Elena Torres <elena.torres@vitalai.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@vitalai.com
Date: 2026-10-12T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Q3 usage report + renewal planning

Jonas / Karthik — thanks for the fast turnaround and the proposal. Procurement prefers a 12-month term with monthly invoicing to keep flexibility. A few clarifying asks from my side before the call:

1) Can you put the staged commit schedule into a table in the PDF so finance can see monthly committed amounts vs expected run-rate?
2) We need a short statement on how burst credits are billed and how quickly they replenish after being used.
3) For the ROI numbers, can you include a sensitivity row that assumes a 15% higher long-chat share (conservative scenario)?

We're good to do the 10/12 10:00AM PT sync — I'll answer procurement follow-ups live. Also looping in our procurement alias to facilitate redlines.

Thanks,
Elena
Head of Product, VitalAI
